title: The WKU Student Handbook
paragraphs: Welcome to WKU — Zhaksylyk Karim University in Uralsk! Every new student receives a copy of the WKU Student Handbook on their first day. The handbook explains the rules, responsibilities, and expectations for all students. Reading it carefully is one of the most important things a new student must do.

Academic rules are taken very seriously at WKU. Students must attend at least 80% of all classes. If you miss more than three consecutive lessons without a valid reason, you must provide a medical certificate or written explanation. Students must not use mobile phones during lectures unless the lecturer gives permission. Academic dishonesty — including plagiarism and cheating in exams — is strictly prohibited. Students who cheat may be expelled from the university.

The campus has specific rules about behaviour and respect. Students must speak politely to all staff and fellow students at all times. You must not make noise in the library, study rooms, or corridors during exam periods. Smoking is prohibited on campus — students who smoke must go to the designated area outside the main gate. Students don't have to wear a uniform, but clothing must be appropriate and respectful.

Dormitory residents have additional responsibilities. You have to sign in and out of the dormitory if you return after 11pm. Guests are allowed until 10pm — they don't have to show identification during daytime hours, but they must register at the reception desk. You shouldn't play loud music after 10pm as it disturbs other residents. The kitchen and common areas must be kept clean at all times.

WKU also has rules about digital conduct. Students must not post disrespectful content about the university or its staff on social media. You should respond to official emails within 24 hours. You must not share your student login details with others. If your device is lost or stolen, you should report it to the IT department immediately.

Finally, WKU encourages students to get involved in campus life. You don't have to join a club or society, but it is strongly recommended. Studies show that students who participate in extracurricular activities perform better academically. You should try at least one new activity each semester. The Student Union office is open every weekday — they will be happy to help you find the right club for your interests.
